questions.stem: Kofi's house number is odd. It is more than 20 and less than 30. The two digits of the number add up to 9. What is Kofi's house number?
questions.solution: The odd numbers from 21 to 29 are 21, 23, 25, 27 and 29. Their digits add up to 3, 5, 7, 9 and 11. Only 27 has digits that add up to 9.

questions.skill: Windows on floors with a changing pattern
questions.stem: A tower has 4 floors. The two lowest floors have 6 windows each. Every floor above them has 2 windows fewer than the floor directly below it. How many windows does the tower have in all?
questions.solution: The floors have 6, 6, then 6 - 2 = 4, then 4 - 2 = 2 windows. 6 + 6 + 4 + 2 = 18.

questions.skill: Working backwards with halves and a gift
questions.stem: Hana had some cards. On Monday she gave away half of her cards. On Tuesday she gave away 3 cards. On Wednesday she gave away half of the cards she still had. Then she had 4 cards left. How many cards did Hana have at the start?
questions.solution: Go backwards. Before Wednesday she had double 4, which is 8. Before Tuesday she had 8 + 3 = 11. Before Monday she had double 11, which is 22.

questions.skill: Wheels of cars, a lorry and bikes
questions.stem: A car park has 2 cars, 1 lorry and some bikes. A car has 4 wheels, a lorry has 6 wheels and a bike has 2 wheels. All the vehicles together have 24 wheels. How many bikes are there?
questions.solution: The 2 cars have 8 wheels and the lorry has 6, so 14 wheels. The bikes have 24 - 14 = 10 wheels. Each bike has 2 wheels, so there are 5 bikes.

questions.skill: Points won and lost by two players
questions.stem: Zoe and Max play 4 rounds of a game. In each round one player wins and the other loses. The winner of a round gets 3 points and the loser loses 1 point. Both start with 0 points. Zoe wins 3 rounds and Max wins 1 round. How many more points does Zoe have than Max?
questions.solution: Zoe won 3 rounds and lost 1: 9 - 1 = 8 points. Max won 1 round and lost 3: 3 - 3 = 0 points. Zoe has 8 more points.

questions.skill: Working backwards with days of the week
questions.stem: Jin says: "Three days before the day before yesterday was Sunday." What day of the week is it today?
questions.solution: The day before yesterday is 2 days ago. Three days before that is 5 days ago. If 5 days ago was Sunday, count 5 days on from Sunday: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday. Today is Friday.

solve.work: Today minus 2 minus 3 = Sunday, so today = Sunday + 5 = Friday.

questions.skill: Two-digit numbers from two digit cards, repeats allowed
questions.stem: Zainab has two digit cards, 4 and 6. She makes two-digit numbers, and she may use the same card in both places. How many different numbers can she make?
questions.solution: The numbers are 44, 46, 64 and 66. That is 4 numbers.

questions.skill: Counting pairs of dancers
questions.stem: Four children, Ali, Bea, Cy and Di, dance in pairs. Every two children dance together exactly once. How many different pairs dance?
questions.solution: Ali dances with Bea, Cy and Di: 3 pairs. Bea dances with Cy and Di: 2 more. Cy dances with Di: 1 more. 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 pairs.

solve.work: AB AC AD BC BD CD.

questions.skill: Which sum of two chosen cards is impossible
questions.stem: Four cards show the numbers 1, 2, 3 and 4. Ola picks two different cards and adds their numbers. Which total can she NOT get?
questions.solution: She can get 1 + 2 = 3, 1 + 4 = 5 and 3 + 4 = 7. The biggest total is 3 + 4 = 7, so 8 is impossible.

questions.skill: Counting routes on a small street grid
questions.stem: Ben walks from home to school. Each step is one block east or one block north. The school is 2 blocks east and 1 block north of home. How many different routes can Ben take?
questions.solution: Ben takes 2 steps east (E) and 1 step north (N). The routes are E E N, E N E and N E E. That is 3 routes.

questions.skill: How many to take to be sure of one
questions.stem: A bag has 4 red balls and 2 green balls, all the same size. You cannot see inside the bag. You take balls out one at a time. How many balls must you take to be sure to have a green ball?
questions.solution: With bad luck the first 4 balls could all be red. The 5th ball must then be green. So you must take 5 balls.

solve.work: Worst case 4 reds first, then the 5th is green.

questions.skill: Fewest boats needed
questions.stem: 17 children go on a river trip. Each boat holds at most 5 children. What is the fewest number of boats needed so that all 17 children can go?
questions.solution: 3 boats hold only 15 children, which is not enough. 4 boats hold 20 children, which is enough. The fewest is 4 boats.

questions.skill: Smallest number from digit cards, no leading zero
questions.stem: Ravi has the cards 4, 0 and 6. He puts all three cards in a row to make a three-digit number. A number cannot start with 0. What is the smallest number he can make?
questions.solution: The first card cannot be 0, so the smallest first card is 4. Then put the smaller card, 0, next and 6 last. The number is 406.

questions.skill: Most money from a few coins
questions.stem: Eva has 4 coins. Each coin is worth 1 euro, 2 euros or 5 euros. What is the most money Eva could have?
questions.solution: She has the most money when all 4 coins are the biggest ones, worth 5 euros each. 4 times 5 = 20 euros.

questions.skill: Pairs of dancers from an odd number of children
questions.stem: 11 children want to dance. Each dancing pair is 2 children. What is the greatest number of pairs that can dance at the same time?
questions.solution: 5 pairs use 10 children. 6 pairs would need 12 children, but there are only 11. So at most 5 pairs can dance.

solve.work: 10 children in 5 pairs, one left over.

questions.skill: Counting two-digit numbers with a digit sum
questions.stem: How many two-digit numbers have two digits that add up to 4? (A two-digit number does not start with 0.)
questions.solution: The numbers are 13, 22, 31 and 40. That is 4 numbers.

questions.skill: How many to take to be sure of two the same colour
questions.stem: A bag holds 4 red, 4 blue and 4 green balls, all the same size. You cannot see inside the bag. How many balls must you take out to be sure that at least two of them have the same colour?
questions.solution: With bad luck the first 3 balls could be red, blue and green, all different. The 4th ball must match one of them. So you must take 4 balls.

solve.work: 3 colours; 3 could all differ, the 4th must match.

questions.skill: Which sum of two chosen cards is impossible
questions.stem: Four cards show the numbers 1, 3, 5 and 7. Lena picks two different cards and adds their numbers. Which total can she NOT get?
questions.solution: She can get 1 + 3 = 4, 3 + 7 = 10 and 5 + 7 = 12. Every card is odd, and two odd numbers always make an even total, so 7 is impossible.

solve.work: Two odd numbers sum to even; totals 4,6,8,10,12; 7 impossible.

questions.skill: Three-digit numbers from three cards including 0
questions.stem: Sam has three cards: 0, 1 and 2. He uses all three cards once to make a three-digit number. A number cannot start with 0. How many different numbers can he make?
questions.solution: The first card is 1 or 2. Starting with 1: 102 and 120. Starting with 2: 201 and 210. That is 4 numbers.

questions.skill: Counting routes on a street grid
questions.stem: Kira walks from home to the park. Each step is one block east or one block north. The park is 2 blocks east and 2 blocks north of her home. How many different routes can Kira take?
questions.solution: Kira takes 2 steps east (E) and 2 steps north (N) in some order. The routes are EENN, ENEN, ENNE, NEEN, NENE and NNEE. That is 6 routes.

questions.skill: Pairs of one boy and one girl
questions.stem: At a dance there are 4 boys and 3 girls. A dancing pair is one boy and one girl. How many different pairs can be made?
questions.solution: Each of the 4 boys can be paired with any of the 3 girls. 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 12 pairs.

questions.skill: The most possible in one place when all are different
questions.stem: 8 ducks swim in 3 ponds. Every pond has at least 1 duck, and no two ponds have the same number of ducks. What is the greatest number of ducks that one pond can have?
questions.solution: To make one pond as full as possible, the other two ponds should have as few ducks as possible. They must be different, so 1 duck and 2 ducks. That leaves 8 - 1 - 2 = 5 ducks.

solve.work: Other two ponds at least 1 and 2; 8-3=5.

questions.skill: How many to take to be sure of two of one kind
questions.stem: A box holds 5 red cards and 3 blue cards, all the same size. You cannot see which card you take. How many cards must you take to be sure that at least 2 of them are red?
questions.solution: With bad luck the first 3 cards could all be blue. After that every card is red, so 2 more cards give 2 red ones. You must take 3 + 2 = 5 cards.

solve.work: Worst: 3 blue + 1 red = 4 with one red; 5th gives 2 reds.

questions.skill: Different sums when a card may be used twice
questions.stem: Ana picks two cards from the cards 1, 2 and 3. She may pick the same card twice. She adds the two numbers. How many different totals can she get?
questions.solution: The totals are 1 + 1 = 2, 1 + 2 = 3, 1 + 3 = 4, 2 + 3 = 5 and 3 + 3 = 6 (2 + 2 = 4 again). The different totals are 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6, which is 5 totals.

questions.skill: Even two-digit numbers from digit cards
questions.stem: Mei has the cards 2, 4 and 5. She makes two-digit numbers using two different cards. How many of these numbers are even?
questions.solution: A number is even when its last digit is 2 or 4. Ending in 2: 42 and 52. Ending in 4: 24 and 54. That is 4 numbers.

questions.skill: The most things that can be bought
questions.stem: A shop has 4 stickers, which cost 2, 3, 4 and 5 euros. Pia has 10 euros. She may buy each sticker at most once. What is the greatest number of stickers she can buy?
questions.solution: She should choose the cheapest stickers. 2 + 3 + 4 = 9 euros, which she can pay. All 4 stickers would cost 14 euros, which is too much. So she can buy 3 stickers.

questions.skill: Counting routes on a grid with a closed crossing
questions.stem: Kira walks from home to the library. Each step is one block east or one block north. The library is 2 blocks east and 3 blocks north of home. The crossing 1 block east and 1 block north of home is closed, so she cannot go through it. How many different routes are there?
questions.solution: Write E for east and N for north. Routes that avoid the closed crossing are EENNN, NNEEN, NNENE and NNNEE. That is 4 routes.

solve.work: 10 routes in all; 2x3=6 pass the closed crossing; 10-6=4.

questions.skill: How many to take to be sure of three the same colour
questions.stem: A bag holds 6 red, 5 blue and 4 green balls, all the same size. You cannot see inside the bag. How many balls must you take out to be sure that at least 3 of them have the same colour?
questions.solution: With bad luck you could take 2 red, 2 blue and 2 green balls, which is 6 balls and no colour has 3. The 7th ball must make 3 of one colour. So you must take 7 balls.

solve.work: Worst 2 of each colour = 6; the 7th makes 3 of one.

questions.skill: Counting two-digit numbers bigger than 30
questions.stem: Ela has the cards 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5. She makes two-digit numbers using two different cards. How many of these numbers are bigger than 30?
questions.solution: The first digit must be 3, 4 or 5. For each first digit there are 4 choices for the second card, because it must be different. 3 times 4 = 12 numbers.

solve.work: Tens digit 3, 4 or 5, each with 4 other units digits: 12.

questions.skill: Number of matches when everyone plays everyone
questions.stem: Five players in a table tennis club play each other exactly once. Each match lasts 10 minutes. The matches are played one after the other with no breaks. How many minutes do all the matches take?
questions.solution: The first player plays 4 matches, the next 3 new ones, then 2, then 1. That is 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10 matches. 10 matches of 10 minutes take 100 minutes.

questions.skill: How many to take to be sure of every kind
questions.stem: A box holds 5 mint, 4 lemon and 3 cherry sweets. They are wrapped the same, so Maya cannot see which flavour she takes. How many sweets must she take to be sure to have at least one of every flavour?
questions.solution: With bad luck she takes all 5 mint and all 4 lemon sweets first, which is 9 sweets and no cherry. The 10th sweet must be cherry. So she must take 10 sweets.

solve.work: Worst: all 5 mint + 4 lemon = 9; 10th is cherry.

questions.skill: Different sums when a number may be used twice
questions.stem: Hassan chooses two cards from the cards 1, 5 and 10. He may choose the same card twice. He adds the two numbers. How many different totals can he get?
questions.solution: The totals are 1 + 1 = 2, 1 + 5 = 6, 1 + 10 = 11, 5 + 5 = 10, 5 + 10 = 15 and 10 + 10 = 20. All 6 are different.

questions.skill: Counting ways to hop along a row
questions.stem: A frog sits on pad 1 of a row of pads numbered 1 to 5. It only moves forward. Each move is either to the next pad or over one pad to the pad after. In how many different ways can the frog get from pad 1 to pad 5?
questions.solution: Write the moves as steps of 1 or 2 that add up to 4: 1+1+1+1, 1+1+2, 1+2+1, 2+1+1 and 2+2. That is 5 ways.

questions.skill: Counting different sums of two chosen cards
questions.stem: Five cards show the numbers 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5. Dev picks two different cards and adds their numbers. How many different totals can he get?
questions.solution: The smallest total is 1 + 2 = 3 and the biggest is 4 + 5 = 9. Every number from 3 to 9 can be made, for example 1+3, 1+4, 1+5, 2+5, 3+5. The totals 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9 make 7 different totals.

questions.skill: The most pairs that can dance at once
questions.stem: A class has 7 boys and 5 girls. In a dance every dancing pair is one boy and one girl. At most how many pairs can dance at the same time?
questions.solution: Every pair needs a girl, and there are only 5 girls. So there can be at most 5 pairs, and 5 boys can be chosen to dance with them.

questions.skill: How many to take to be sure of a left and a right
questions.stem: A box holds 4 left-hand gloves and 4 right-hand gloves, all of the same colour and style. It is dark, so you cannot see which glove you take. How many gloves must you take to be sure to have a left glove and a right glove?
questions.solution: With bad luck the first 4 gloves could all be left-hand gloves. The 5th glove must then be a right-hand glove. So you must take 5 gloves.

solve.work: Worst: all 4 of one hand, the 5th is the other.
